subject: Coordination: MSA + Order Form — IP indemnity carve-out and litigation exposure
messages:
From: Suzanne Lambert <suzanne.lambert@acmedata.com>

Cc: contracts@acmedata.com
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME redlines — IP indemnity carve-out to liability cap (MSA + OF)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team ran a quick review and returned a set of redlines (attached). The key item we need to close is the liability cap carve-out for IP infringement. Our proposed language (excerpted below) is: "Notwithstanding Section 12 (Limitation of Liability), liability arising from a third-party claim of intellectual property infringement for which Supplier indemnifies Customer under Section 8 shall not be subject to the liability cap."

From ACME's perspective this cannot be limited to a small monetary cap — an IP claim could require injunctive relief or significant indemnity payments. We are open to narrow tailoring (e.g., excluding willful infringement, capping at insurance limits, or requiring notice and cooperation), but removing the carve-out entirely isn't acceptable.

Please review and let us know Redwood's position. We prefer to resolve the indemnity interplay in the MSA rather than a side letter.

Attachment: ACME_MSA_Redlines_2026-07-05.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Suzanne Lambert
Sr. Contracts Manager, Acme Data Systems
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: ACME redlines — IP indemnity carve-out to liability cap (MSA + OF)

Marissa / legal team — forwarding ACME's redlines and the core ask: they want the IP indemnity to sit outside the overall liability cap (i.e., unlimited/uncapped). See Suzanne's note attached.

Quick summary of our negotiating levers:
- Mutuality: ask them to make the carve-out mutual (both parties) — ACME will resist but worth trying.
- Insurance backstop: require proof of IP insurance or build a cap equal to insured limits.
- Carve-out scope: limit to direct indemnity payments only, exclude punitive/consequential (we keep consequential damages excluded elsewhere).
- Remedies: preserve our ability to seek injunctive relief and exclude that from indemnity exposure if it's not a monetary claim.
- Escrow/limitation: if they insist on uncapped exposure, request a monetary cap tied to the deal value or a hard cap (e.g., $5M) plus insurance.

Action items: Laura, can you draft a redline that: (1) offers a mutual IP carve-out; (2) if they won't accept mutuality, proposes a compromise of "IP indemnity not subject to liability cap, provided indemnitor's exposure is limited to insurance proceeds and direct damages up to $5M" (we can pick the cap in negotiation); and (3) clarifies that consequential and punitive damages remain excluded.

Marissa — flag to sales that this is a legal risk conversation (ACME is a mid-size enterprise, renewal + upsell pipeline).

Thanks, Vivek
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: ACME redlines — IP indemnity carve-out to liability cap (MSA + OF)

Vivek / Marissa — drafting note and recommended approach below. I attach a short internal risk summary (Risk_Summary_IP_Exposure.xlsx).

Recommended commercial compromise (reasoned position):
1) Mutuality: propose the carve-out language to be mutual by default. If ACME declines to make it mutual, we consider a single-sided carve-out ONLY where it is constrained by (2) and (3).
2) Insurance-first approach: IP indemnity recoveries shall be payable first from indemnitor's valid, collectible IP insurance. Require evidence of insurance (policy declarations).
3) Monetary safety valve: where insurance is absent or insufficient, cap Redwood's exposure for monetary indemnity payments at $5,000,000 for the relevant claim or series of related claims.
4) Direct damages only: recoverable amounts limited to direct indemnity payments; consequential, punitive and speculative damages remain excluded.
5) Procedural protections: (i) prompt notice and a right to control defense; (ii) obligations to cooperate; (iii) ability to settle with consent (cannot accept injunctive terms that materially impair our service without further approval).

Draft language (high level): "Subject to Section X (Procedures for Handling Claims), indemnity obligations for third-party claims of intellectual property infringement shall not be governed by the limitation of liability set forth in Section 12, provided that (a) recoveries shall be payable first from the indemnitor's IP insurance and (b) monetary indemnity payments not recovered from insurance shall be capped at $5,000,000 for any single claim or series of related claims. Consequential and punitive damages remain excluded."

Rationale: This preserves ACME's need for meaningful IP remediation while capping purely monetary exposure and leveraging insurance as the primary source of recovery. It also gives us procedural protections to manage litigation risk.

Next steps: Vivek / Marissa, if you agree I will prepare a tracked-redline MSA and a short comment memo for sales to present to ACME. If they push back on insurance evidence, we can offer a one-time escrow or increase the cap for strategic accounts.

- Laura
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Suzanne Lambert <suzanne.lambert@acmedata.com>

Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: ACME redlines — IP indemnity carve-out to liability cap (MSA + OF)

Vivek — appreciate the quick turnaround and Laura, thanks for the thoughtful compromise language. ACME prefers a party-unilateral carve-out (i.e., Redwood's indemnity for Redwood-originating IP exposure not subject to cap) but we can consider mutual language if Redwood can show we have comparable exposure (we do not).

On the proposed insurance-first + $5M monetary backstop: ACME legal will need to review internally. A few items we will likely push on: (1) preference that the cap be per-claim without aggregation; (2) insistence that injunctive relief not be limited by the cap; and (3) if insurance is the primary source, a floor/retention cannot reduce our recovery (i.e., we resist a captive retention that nullifies coverage).

We are available for a short call tomorrow to go through these points. Could Redwood confirm who will be on the call from legal and sales? Also please send your tracked redline when ready.

Best,
Suzanne
Sr. Contracts Manager, Acme Data Systems
